flashcard_questions.q: What name is given to the monarch's personal right to call Parliament and declare war?
About how many advisors sat on Elizabeth's Privy Council?
How many councillors had Mary I used, compared with Elizabeth's much smaller council?
Which Privy Council role was the chief advisor, through whom all the Queen's letters passed?
Which Privy Council role controlled access to the Queen and booked her appointments?
Who served Elizabeth as her most trusted advisor for 40 years?
Which of Elizabeth's advisors built the spy network that uncovered Catholic plots?
How many years did Elizabeth wait before adding Robert Dudley to the Privy Council?
How many times did Elizabeth call Parliament during her 45-year reign?
What were the local gentry called who enforced the law unpaid in their county?
How many Justices of the Peace served across England under Elizabeth?
What was the smallest number of Justices of the Peace needed to pass a death sentence?
Which nobles were appointed by the Queen to raise militia and collect taxes in an area?
What name was given to Elizabeth's summer tours staying in nobles' homes?
What term describes giving jobs, land and titles to keep supporters loyal?

notes: 15 cards: 6 statistic, 4 role or term to definition, 3 person to significance, 2 institution. Left the social-order hierarchy out because any card on it would be a list; the Privy Council control tactics are causal essay material, not cards.
